cells.tense: Present — you're here, and the pen is in your hand.
cells.verb: holding the line you chose, with everything you gathered behind it
cells.place: where the scales get set right and what's out of proportion gets adjusted
cells.ask: If you want it, there's room to let the people around you in on what the standing-firm was for — not to recruit them, just so the sense of it travels past you. What comes back is this: direction that moves from what you actually feel, not from the pressure against it.
cells.core: You're holding your ground where it counts, and you're holding it fairly. The push against you hasn't made you grab more than your share, and it hasn't made you give up the share that's yours — you're defending a line you actually drew, and you can say why it sits where it sits. That's the rare version: steady without getting hard, firm without tipping the scale. Nothing here is asking you to change it. It's only pointing at what it's free to feed next: the sense of it doesn't have to live inside you alone. Let the people around you see what the standing-firm was for, in your words, so it becomes something they can carry too, in theirs.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding a fair line, and it's yours — it could be shared now, not just defended.

cells.tense: Future — you're already braced for a fight that hasn't been scheduled.
cells.verb: defending the line past the point where anyone is pushing on it
cells.place: where the scales get set right — and keep getting leaned on
cells.ask: Before the next push, let the whole picture sit in front of you for a minute — every piece of it, including the parts that aren't a threat — and let the stillness do the weighing instead of the muscle. What comes back is movement that starts from what you actually feel about this, not from what you're bracing against.
cells.core: You're defending a line that nobody is currently crossing. Somewhere ahead there's a version of this where you get overruled or shorted, and you're living in that room already — so every exchange reads as the opening move, and you meet it with everything you've got. The trouble is that a scale can't settle while a hand is pressing on one side of it. The steadiness you gathered was supposed to be in service of something fair; right now it's in service of the bracing. The way out isn't less of you. It's letting the whole thing — the real pressure and the imagined kind, the parts that are yours and the parts that aren't — sit quietly in view until you can tell them apart.
cells.sheetLine: You're guarding the scale so hard it can't settle.

cells.tense: Past — still standing at a door that's already closed behind you.
cells.verb: letting the line slip because gathering yourself up again feels too far away
cells.place: where the scales get set right — and have gone quiet
cells.ask: Rather than forcing yourself to stand firm, name what already ended here, out loud, and keep one thing it left you — a shape, a lesson, a plain fact about what's yours. Hold that, and the steadiness tends to follow it back. What comes back is direction that moves from what you feel, not from what you're avoiding.
cells.core: You know what's fair here, and you've stopped holding to it. Something back there ended — a fight you didn't win, a line that didn't hold — and part of you is still standing at that door, so the momentum that would carry you into this one never quite gathers. It's not that you stopped caring whether things are even. It's that defending it started to feel like more than you had. Pushing harder won't fill that; it's the empty place, and effort poured straight in just drains out. What fills it is behind you, not ahead: treat the ending as finished, honor it, and keep what it produced. Steadiness has something to stand on once the past is allowed to be the past.
cells.sheetLine: You know what's fair and you've quit holding to it.

cells.tense: Disowned present — the pen's moving, and you've set it down in your mind.
cells.verb: holding your ground and calling it just how things fell out
cells.place: where the scales get set right, by a hand that won't say it's yours
cells.ask: Something already cleared here because you stood where you stood. Take one piece of what that clearing revealed and build one plain, deliberate thing on it — and put your name on the building. What comes back is movement you can feel as yours, direction from genuine engagement instead of from a line you keep pretending you didn't draw.
cells.core: You're already defending a line, and it's a fair one — people can feel exactly where you stand on what's even and what isn't, and they adjust around it. But you'd describe yourself as just going along, as if the scale balanced on its own. It didn't. You gathered yourself and held, and the holding is doing real work. What's missing isn't the determination; it's your name on it. Here's the simpler thing underneath: some structure already came down because you stood where you stood, and there's open ground now that didn't exist before. Build something on it on purpose — small, yours, in the daylight — and the author of the holding stops being anonymous.
cells.sheetLine: You're already holding the fair line. You just won't say you drew it.
